title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Former Costa Mesa police officer Robert Jay Josett, 35, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors after harassing a former mistress and misusing police databases. Starting in April 2024 after she ended the relationship, he sent thousands of texts, calls, and social media messages over nine months, sometimes more than 100 contacts in one day, and called her and her new boyfriend up to 58 times in a single day. He also made 13 unauthorized searches in a California law enforcement database on his mistress, a romantic rival, and his wife, and used the department's license plate reader system to track vehicles, including after he was placed on leave.

On June 28, 2024, Josett was served with a protective order and notice of termination, then drove by the woman's home and was arrested. He was sentenced to three years informal probation and a domestic violence program lasting 52 weeks, and he had already spent nine months on a GPS ankle monitor. His law enforcement certification review by California's Peace Officers Standards and Training is pending.
